findings.title: ensure_loaded! is only called for the controller's locale; other entry points are unprotected
Initializer depends on file load order and the backend class, and has a fragile hash-subclass design

response:
## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: ensure_loaded! is only called for the controller's locale; other entry points are unprotected

Affected:
- app/controllers/application_controller.rb:158-159
- lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:62-65

Explanation:
`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is called only in the controller's `set_locale`. Jobs, mailers, and the console never call it, so the fallback locales (the site default and `:en`) may not be loaded there. The `translate` accelerator loads only `config.locale`, so fallback lookups in those contexts can miss translations or return "translation missing". `ensure_loaded!` is also called on every request. It is cheap when the locale is already loaded, but it builds arrays and does `Array#include?` lookups each time. The fix is to make `translate` itself ensure the fallback locales are loaded, or to call `ensure_loaded!` wherever the locale is set outside controllers, such as the job and mailer entry points.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
# in translate_accelerator, before lookup
load_locale(config.locale) unless @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)
I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! if I18n.respond_to?(:fallbacks)
~~~

## 2) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Initializer depends on file load order and the backend class, and has a fragile hash-subclass design

Affected:
- config/initializers/i18n.rb:1-24

Explanation:
The "order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb" comment is not enforced, since the file is named `i18n.rb` and Rails loads initializers alphabetically. The `I18n.ensure_loaded!` call it relies on exists only if the translate_accelerator patch has been loaded.

`I18n.backend.class.send(:include, ...)` instantiates the backend and patches whatever class it happens to be. This is fragile if the backend is later swapped out.

`FallbackLocaleList < Hash` overrides only `[]`, so other Hash methods such as `fetch` and `key?` behave inconsistently. `SiteSetting.default_locale` is also read at initializer time and at runtime. If the DB is unavailable or the setting is nil, `.to_sym` raises `NoMethodError`.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_s.presence&.to_sym, :en].compact.uniq
~~~

Also rename the file so it sorts after the freedom patches, for example `03-i18n.rb`, and include the module in `I18n::Backend::Simple` explicitly.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).
